61: Credits received per day when this outfit is in active use.
62: Allows scanning of your target ship's outfits from up to this distance away.
63: Allows scanning of your target ship's outfits. The range of this outfit scanner is proportional to the square root of this value.
64: Determines how long it takes to perform an outfit scan. A higher value will correspond to a quicker scan.
65: The maximum speed of this outfit scanner is proportional to the square root of this value. The observed scan speed will be impacted by multiple factors. Targets which are farther away or have a larger outfit capacity will take longer to scan.
66: Increases the time required for other ships to perform an outfit scan of this ship. A value of one has the same influence on the time taken as adding one more ton of outfit space to scan.
67: Tons of general-purpose space this outfit provides.
68: Tons of general-purpose space this outfit uses up. Some outfits also use up weapon space or engine space.
69: Tons of space this ship has for outfits (including weapons and engines).
70: Hull damage taken per second when overheated. Overheat damage scales with how far past the overheat threshold the ship is.
71: Increases the percentage past overheated at which point overheat damage begins.
72: Reduces the ability of optical-guided missiles to track your ship, which is mostly useful for larger ships. The more optical jamming is installed, the greater the distance at which missiles can be jammed, and the greater the chance that a jammed missile will fly off in a random direction.
73: Influences the tracking strength of optical-guided missiles targeting this ship. A larger value means the ship is easier to track.
74: Percentage of this weapon's damage that leaks through to the hull while the target's shields are still active.
75: Protection provided against piercing weapons. Increases by the given factor the amount of piercing required to make the same portion of weapon damage bypass a ship's shields.
76: Piercing damage resisted on all incoming projectiles, preventing damage from leaking through the shields to the hull.
77: Reduces the ability of radar-guided missiles to track your ship. The more radar jamming is installed, the greater the distance at which missiles can be jammed, and the greater the chance that a jammed missile will fly off in a random direction.
78: Replenishes fuel by harvesting the stellar wind. Ramscoops are more effective when closer to a star. If you add more than one ramscoop, each additional one is less effective: you need four ramscoops to achieve double the recharge rate that one ramscoop provides.
79: Crew members required to operate this ship, and the total number bunks available. Extra bunks can be used for passengers or extra crew.
80: Changes the number of crew members this ship requires by this amount.
81: Changes the number of crew members this ship requires by this amount. Mandatory crew cannot be replaced by automation.
82: Reverse thrust generated by engines. Reverse thrust allows a ship to slow down without needing to turn around.
83: Energy consumed per second when firing reverse thrusters.
84: Heat produced per second when firing reverse thrusters.
85: Shield damage dealt to the ship per second when firing reverse thrusters.
86: Hull damage dealt to the ship per second when firing reverse thrusters.
87: Fuel consumed per second when firing reverse thrusters.
88: Accumulated shield discharging per second when firing reverse thrusters.
89: Accumulated hull corrosion per second when firing reverse thrusters.
90: Accumulated ionization per second when firing reverse thrusters.
